notes: Derivation from the read lineage-reads-1985/s-101.json: CONFORMS on a unpopulatable-antecedent derivation of its own (docs/CONFORMANCE.md section 8, DRV-1985-GR-IV.4.1-p2); the code location is where the compiler meets the rule's subject. The read: The antecedent ('Certain of the characters comprising the COBOL character set may not be graphically represented in definitions of national and international standard character sets. In these instances ...') holds only for a source character set that lacks a graphic for a COBOL character. Source bytes become characters in exactly one place, SourceTextDecoder.Decode, and its result is one of a closed set of readings: a mark-named UTF-8/UTF-16/UTF-32 (or Malformed, which yields no text and the error COBOL5434), unmarked UTF-8, or ISO/IEC 8859-1. Every one of them contains the 78 characters of the glossary's COBOL character set (digits, both cases of letters, space and + - * / = $ , ; . " ( ) > < :) at U+0020-U+007A, so no COBOL character is ever unrepresented and no substitute graphic exists for a program to use or observe; the implementation specifies none. This corrects the s-99 draft's names, which grounded the claim on ISO 646 IRV: the glossary itself notes that the 1973 IRV shows the currency sign as ¤, so IRV is NOT a set that represents every COBOL character; the claim holds because the decoder's readings are UCS and Latin-1, where U+0024 is $. The 2023 sibling DRV-GR-8.1.3.2-5 (docs/conformance/8) closes by the same arm on the same mechanism. Witnessed on the train85b-rows build: E:/COBOL-coord/scratch/w20262131/last2/probes/cset85.cob uses all 78 characters of the 1985 COBOL character set in program text outside literals (lowercase and uppercase words, digits, space, + - * / = in COMPUTE, $ and , . in a PICTURE, ; and , as separators, " as literal delimiter, ( ) : in a reference modifier, > < in a condition) and runs identically in all three reading families: unmarked UTF-8 (runs/cset85-001), UTF-16LE with mark (probes/cset85u16.cob, runs/cset85u16-001) and ISO/IEC 8859-1 (probes/cset85l1.cob, an 0xA4 byte in a comment line forces the Latin-1 reading and draws COBOL5435; runs/cset85l1-001): each prints ARITH OK +0619, EDIT $1,234.50, REFMOD 2345 and the 52 letters, exit 0.
